newsitem.title: USA: Icahn seeks three Panaco board seats.
newsitem.headline: Icahn seeks three Panaco board seats.

text.p: Wall Street investor Carl Icahn said on Tuesday he is seeking to fill all three currently vacant seats on Panaco Inc's board of directors.

The investor, who holds a 12.8 percent stake or three million shares in Panaco, said in a special notice that his firm will appear at the company's 1997 annual stockholder meeting to elect nominees to fill the vacant seats, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
"Icahn & Co is proposing to nominate three nominees for election to the board," Icahn wrote, adding that he reserves the right to increase that number if the board increases the number of vacancies.

"The number of nominees proposed to be nominated at the annual meeting by Icahn & Co. will, in no event, be less than the number of nominees which the management of the corporation proposes to nominate," Icahn wrote.
Icahn said the reason for nominating the new slate of directors is to maximize stockholder value through various means, which might include merging the company with National Energy Group Inc

Icahn's nominees are: Harold First, a New York financial consultant; Jouko Tamminen, who works for Icahn Associates Corp; and Theodore Altman, an attorney with the firm Gordon Altman Butowsky Weitzen Shalov & Wein.
Panaco, with headquarters in Kansas City, is in the crude petroleum and natural gas business.
On Tuesday, Panaco shares last traded at 3 7/8.
